messages:
Lee (support): FYI opened a ticket with Acme about a billing mismatch. They say their Dedicated dashboard shows ~120 reserved GPU hours used this month but invoice lists 150 reserved hours charged. Customer: INV-9876, tenant acme-ai.
Maria (billing): thanks. do we have the raw metering export for acme for the invoice period? need to check attribution between reserved vs burst pools.
Lee (support): I pulled the billing export (s3://billing-exports/2026-02/acme-invoice-INV-9876.csv) and pushed it to the support bucket. attaching summary: reserved_hours=120, burst_hours=10, invoice_charged_reserved=150.
Ajay (eng-runtime): that smells like a misattribution. any logs showing fallback models or autoscale events during the period? if a request falls back to a cheaper variant we sometimes route to burst cluster and attribution should reflect that.
Sara (dedicated-ops): checked autoscaler events: there was a spike on 2026-02-14 03:12 -> 03:19 UTC with scale-up failures, many requests fell into burst-capacity for ~7m. burst pool reported 10h total cumulative for the tenant.
Lee (support): customer insists tokens (embedding+generation) counts in their app match dashboard counts but invoice differs. they provided a sample request id: req_7b2f1c. Can we repro attribution for that request?
Ajay (eng-runtime): looking up req_7b2f1c in request-logs. here's the request path we record:
```
2026-02-14T03:13:07Z tenant=acme request=req_7b2f1c model=gpt-small variant=v1 routed=dedicated-pool-3 -> fallback=basic-burst-pool token_in=412 token_out=228
```
Ajay (eng-runtime): meter-attribution service should have marked that as burst tokens. i'll query the usage table for that request id.
Ajay (eng-runtime): SQL I ran:
```
SELECT tenant, pool_type, sum(tokens) FROM usage_tokens
WHERE request_id = 'req_7b2f1c' GROUP BY tenant, pool_type;
```
Ajay (eng-runtime): result showed pool_type='reserved' tokens=640. so attribution was incorrectly recorded as reserved even though routing shows fallback to burst.
Maria (billing): that explains it — reserved usage inflated by those fallback requests. how many requests in the spike window were misattributed?
Ajay (eng-runtime): quick aggregate:
```
SELECT pool_type, count(*), sum(tokens) FROM usage_tokens
WHERE tenant='acme' AND ts >= '2026-02-14T03:10:00Z' AND ts <= '2026-02-14T03:20:00Z'
GROUP BY pool_type;
```
Ajay (eng-runtime): result: reserved: count=3, sum_tokens=2200 ; burst: count=0, sum_tokens=0. But router logs show ~150 requests went to burst. so batch job that writes attribution entries failed during that period.
Sara (dedicated-ops): I see an error in attribution-writer logs around 03:15 UTC: NullPointer when resolving pool_id for fallback routes. stacktrace points to commit 9a1f3c in attribution-service.
Lee (support): is this a recent regression? did the commit land in production before the invoice period?
Ajay (eng-runtime): commit 9a1f3c was deployed 2026-02-12 as part of faster-routing change. it added a new routing tag but didn't handle missing pool metadata when fallback happens.
Maria (billing): estimate impact: if burst hours were recorded as reserved for the whole spike, that could add ~30 reserved hours to their usage. we need to compute exact hours and propose a credit.
Ajay (eng-runtime): I ran a corrected attribution pipeline (replay) over the 10-minute window and got corrected numbers: reserved_hours=120 (unchanged baseline) + 0 extra, burst_hours=10. invoice currently shows reserved_hours=150 because the buggy entries were counted in the reserved bucket during billing aggregation.
Lee (support): plan: 1) fix attribution bug (patch + hotfix deploy) 2) replay/generate corrected metering export 3) issue billing credit for misattributed reserved hours and update invoice. ok?
Sara (dedicated-ops): patch ready (PR: github.com/redwood/attribution/PR/215). will deploy to prod after smoke test. added a guard for missing pool metadata.
BillingBot: Billing export regeneration started for INV-9876 (job id regen-8721). Estimated time 12m.
Maria (billing): once regen completes, I'll calculate delta and propose a credit note. preliminary credit: 30 reserved GPU hours refunded -> credit amount $4,500 (per contract rate). I'll confirm.
Lee (support): notified customer (Acme) that we're investigating and will provide an official credit and corrected invoice. they asked for ETA; told them 24-48h. they appreciated the update :thumbsup:
Ajay (eng-runtime): follow-up: root cause — attribution-service did lookups against pool metadata service; when fallback routing happens the pool metadata key is different (we used new tag) and the lookup returned null, writer defaulted to reserved_pool id. fixed to default to 'burst' when fallback tag present and fail loudly if unknown.
Sara (dedicated-ops): deployed hotfix at 2026-02-14T04:05Z, smoke tests passed. added alert to attribution-writer for null pool resolutions. alert rule: high error rate in attribution-writer for >1m.
Maria (billing): regen done. new numbers: invoice corrected reserved_hours=120, burst_hours=10. issuing credit INV-9876-C1 amount $4,500 and sending corrected invoice INV-9876-v2 to Acme. CC'ing legal for audit trail.
Lee (support): customer confirmed receipt and says dashboard now matches updated invoice. closing loop with Acme.
Ajay (eng-runtime): created postmortem INT-4321 with timeline and mitigation steps. will follow up with a small end-to-end unit test to catch this regression in CI.
Maria (billing): marking ticket resolved and noting manual credit applied. will include memo for finance reconciliation.
Lee (support): thanks all. saving thread into support/ for future reference and linking INT-4321.
Maria (billing): action items assigned: Maria -> issue credit and send corrected invoice; Ajay -> merge PR and add CI test; Sara -> monitor attribution-writer alerts for 48h.
BillingBot: Ticket INT-4321 created and linked to invoice INV-9876.
